relevance_note: Clinical note on two Italian brothers with SSADH deficiency and ALDH5A1 missense variants: "two affected siblings born of healthy nonconsanguineous Italian parents".
method_note: The Markdown file is a journal PDF that also contains two unrelated Clinical/Scientific Notes (palinacousis after temporal ICH; adult-onset Alexander disease with a GFAP variant); those were ignored as out of scope. Labels 'Case 1'/'Case 2' follow the text (the table uses bare '1','2' under 'Patients', which the text calls Case 1 and Case 2). Rows were written by hand in a short Python script in scratch; all spans checked verbatim by script. The table's ALDH5A1 genotype cell is filled only in row 1 (Case 1: 'c.278G>T (p.C93F) c.526G>A (p.G176R)'); row 2 (Case 2) is empty in the converted file. Case 2's variants were recorded from the text sentence about 'our cases' plus the cDNA strings in the Discussion ('c.278G>T (exon 1) and c.526G>A (exon 3)'); no protein change is given for Case 2 there, so protein is null. The Markdown renders '>' as '>' in the text; values use '>'. Zygosity not stated (compound heterozygosity is not written; the paper only says 'patients homozygous for the two mutations were severely affected', about other patients), so 'not reported'. Variant type 'missense' from 'The missense alterations ... in our cases' (named group: both siblings). Functional evidence from expression-study sentence naming each cDNA variant. No parental testing reported; healthy untested parents get no rows. MRI T2 signal increase of pallidum and dentatum is stated for both cases by name. Normal MR spectroscopy and the normal 46 XY karyotype are not attributed to a named case, so no rows. Urinary/plasma GHB values (table) were not recorded as features because the paper does not state they are elevated per person. PED (paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia) was mapped to checklist 'exertional dyskinesia' and 'dystonia'. Case 1 'hyperactivity' was recorded as a feature but not mapped to 'attention problems or ADHD'. Case 1 'clumsiness' mapped to 'gross or fine motor deficits'. Case 1 language: 'dysarthria' and 'the language disorder'. Ages: 18-year-old and 13-year-old taken as age at report; exam ages 16 and 12. No contradictions found.
